join.termsTitle: Rules for supporters and organizations (key points)

terms.age: You can act as a supporter only if you are 18 or older
terms.purpose: Use what people write and their nicknames only to support them, and never share them
terms.inApp: Talk inside the app and don't ask for the person's contact details
terms.sensitive: Requests about life or violence and from people under 18 go only to organizations we have interviewed
terms.realName: An individual supporter's real name is shared with the people they offer to help and organizations they raise their hand for
terms.records: Contribution records belong to you and are all deleted if you leave
terms.stop: If the rules aren't followed, samasama may suspend use

join.flowTitle: How to become a supporting organization

flow.interview: Have an interview with samasama (about 60 minutes online)
flow.approved: Once approved, you're listed and can make offers

join.appliedBody: The samasama team will contact you to set up an interview. After the interview you can make offers.
join.skillsNote: Area names differ depending on who asked
join.checksTitle: Six points we will talk about in the interview
join.checksTip: These are the points samasama checks in the interview. Choose the answer closest to how you think now, and add a few words where you can. We will use what you write here in the interview. Choosing "I'd like to talk about it" does not by itself mean your application will be turned down.

selfCheck.discuss: I'd like to talk about it

care.statement: We agree that people can care for strangers and people outside their family, even without being paid
care.note: This does not mean working unpaid forever or making all support free.
care.prompt: How do you think about supporting someone you have never met, who is not family, and from whom you get no thanks or reward? (optional)

imagine.statement: We have faced problems that were not our own fault, or we can imagine such situations from the point of view of the person in them
imagine.note: You do not need to write about painful experiences. A situation you can picture, or an imagined one, is fine.
imagine.prompt: How would you like to face people who are struggling for reasons they cannot change on their own? (optional)

consulteeFirst.statement: When our organization's interests and the better choice for the person asking for help conflict, we can put that person first
consulteeFirst.note: This does not deny the income or salaries your work needs. We ask how you think when interests conflict.
consulteeFirst.prompt: When the choice that brings income differs from the better choice for the person asking, how do you decide? (optional)

activity.statement: We can describe our current work in concrete terms, or explain in our own words whose difficulties we want to face from now on
activity.note: Organizations that are just getting started can apply too.
activity.prompt: Tell us about your current work. If you are just starting, tell us who you want to help, what you want to do, and why. (optional)

direct.statement: We are an organization that directly supports the people who have the problem
direct.note: If you do not work with people directly (for example grants, research, publicity or training for organizations), we will suggest other ways to take part in the interview.
direct.prompt: After you connect with the person asking for help, what will your organization do for them? Who will handle it? (optional)

barriers.statement: We care that barriers such as distance, organizational boundaries and language get in the way of support, and we want a society where support reaches across them
barriers.note: You do not need to have overcome these barriers already.
barriers.prompt: Tell us about barriers you feel in your work, and the support you would like to give if they disappeared. (optional)

proxy.title: Register a request on behalf

proxy.name: The person's nickname
proxy.words: In their words (as you heard them)
proxy.consent: The person agreed to registering this request here
proxy.submit: Register and show the handover code
proxy.required: Please fill in the required fields
proxy.notApproved: You can register on behalf of someone once the interview with the samasama team is done and your organization is approved.
proxy.codeTip: When the person has a phone, they can enter this code to make the request their own. Until then, offers and messages come to your organization's proxy requests.
proxy.handOnPaper: Write this code on paper and give it to the person (valid until {date}). Once you close this screen, it can't be shown again.
proxy.print: Print a sheet for the person
proxy.noneIsOk: If nothing fits, you can continue without picking.

contrib.title: My contributions
contrib.keep: These records stay even if your affiliation changes. The content of requests is not kept (only indicators and your affiliation at the time). Everything is deleted if you leave.
contrib.thanksArrived: Thanks from the person who asked
contrib.resolvedRecord: {count, plural, =0 {A request was solved} one {A request was solved (# confirmed indicator)} other {A request was solved (# confirmed indicators)}}
contrib.growth: +{month} in the last 30 days ・ +{year} in the last year
contrib.howCounted: We count each request that the person confirmed as resolved, one by one. A company or community request also counts as one. We don't multiply by the number of people, and offers or quick replies don't add to it. Only indicators confirmed by samasama are counted, and thank-yous are counted separately. The indicators are based on the SDG global indicators, but this way of counting is samasama's own and is not set or endorsed by the United Nations or anyone else.
contrib.worldHint: Tap an indicator to see it in the context of the world
contrib.loadFailed: Couldn't load. Please try again later

invitations.title: {name} has invited you
invitations.lead: If you accept, you can support requests as a member of this organization. You also agree to the rules for supporters and organizations.
invitations.underAge: You can accept this as a supporter from age 18. You can still decline it.

org.membersTip: Requests and messages belong to the organization. Only current members can read them; removed members lose access from that day. Contribution records stay with each person.
org.inviteTip: Invite with the person's own email (not a shared department address). If they have an account the invitation reaches them; otherwise it appears when they sign up.
org.rolesTip: Manager: edits the organization's profile, contact and areas, and invites, removes or changes the role of members. Member: makes offers and talks with people on behalf of the organization. Managers can support requests just like members.
org.lastOwner: You can't remove the last manager. Make someone else a manager first
org.contactEmailHint: Where the team sends notices. Not used to sign in
org.populationHint: Used when you ask as a company or community (for contribution counts)
org.areasTip: Find shows requests from these areas (turn on “Include requests I can support remotely” to also see requests from outside them). They are also shown on your public organization page. Until you choose, the area from your application is used.
org.areasFromApplication: Using the area from your application

world.title: See it in the world
world.about: "Most it could reach" is the number if the problem spread as far as it could in the world (for a personal problem, the world population). "Facing it now" is the number of people facing the problem in the world today. "Resolved through samasama" is the number of requests resolved through samasama. The goal is zero, where the problem no longer exists. The circles are not drawn to scale.
world.diagramLabel: A diagram with the people facing it now inside the most it could reach, and the requests resolved through samasama inside that
world.insideOutTitle: Build up resolutions to the size of the world
world.insideOut: Add resolutions one by one, widening what samasama can reach (inside-out)
world.outsideInTitle: Make the problem disappear from the world
world.outsideIn: From the world's side, bring the problem itself closer to zero (outside-in)
world.growth: +{month} in the last 30 days ・ +{year} in the last year
world.footnote: "Most it could reach" and "facing it now" are statistics from the UN and others; "resolved through samasama" is the number of resolutions added up one by one. We show it as resolutions added up, not as an estimate. This way of counting is samasama's own and is not set or endorsed by the United Nations or anyone else.
world.loadFailed: Couldn't load. Please try again later

facingNote.share: {year} ・ the share from {source} (UN SDG database) multiplied by the world population of the same year ・ {full} people
facingNote.lacking: {year} ・ people without access, worked out from the share with access from {source} (UN SDG database) ・ {full} people

world.facingUnknownNote: We haven't yet found a published figure for the number of people facing this problem. We'll add it when we do.
world.goalNote: The problem no longer exists in the world. The SDG targets say things like "halve it", but samasama aims for zero.
